Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
942 AM EST Fri Nov 13 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...

No substantial changes as of this morning. Maintaining drier 
trends for Td over the next couple of days.  

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) First snowfall for parts of the Alleghenies with spotty
  showers & brisk conditions elsewhere through Saturday. 

- 2) Below normal temperatures and dry condtions are expected 
  Monday and Tuesday before a warm up occurs.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1... First snowfall for parts of the Alleghenies with 
spotty showers & brisk conditions elsewhere through Saturday.

Latest surface analyses and satellite data depict low pressure
moving well off to our northeast and occluding off the NJ/NY
coast. Any lingering showers have cleared for the moment as most
precipitation remains to the northeast closer to the center low,
with numerous pieces of upper-level energy rotating about its 
axis. 

One of these pieces of energy moves through later this 
morning, and interacts with the aforementioned occluding 
boundary offshore. This may be enough to throw some showers back
into northeast MD on the back side of the departing low. 
Otherwise, most areas likely stay mostly dry for much of the 
day. As flow turns more northwesterly aloft throughout the day, 
we start to get a bit more of a connection to the moisture 
source off the Great Lakes moving towards the Allegheny Front. 
This will lead to another round of upslope snow shower activity 
by tonight into early Saturday. These will of course be 
maximized at elevations above 2000 feet and in particular the 
upslope favored zones of western Garrett, western Pendleton, and
western Grant counties. If travel disruptions were to 
materializes, expect impacts to US-219 from the MD/PA line to WV
line, US-48 from Mount Storm, WV west to Davis, WV, and US-33 
west of Franklin, WV. Snow accumulations will remain on the 
order of a coating to 2" with the greater probabilities of 1-2" 
with localized 3" amounts above 3000 feet pending any 
squalls/streamers (mainly late Friday night through Saturday 
midday).


KEY MESSAGE 2...Below normal temperatures and dry condtions are 
expected Monday and Tuesday before a warm up occurs.

Heights will start rising Monday as the amplified upper level 
patterns slowly progresses eastward. Winds should be much less 
noticeable by Monday and Tuesday as the surface high finally reaches 
the Mid Atlantic, although temperatures remain below normal. Given 
the lighter winds, the subsequent nights could turn out colder in 
many areas, with widespread near or below freezing temperatures 
outside of the urban centers and tidal shoreline. Since this will be 
more than two weeks after the average first freeze, no frost/freeze 
headlines will be issued.

Further upper level amplification will likely happen toward mid 
week. While a trough or low could develop toward the southeast 
coast, it appears that ridging will dominate the Mid Atlantic, 
maintaining dry conditions through next week. The ridging will also 
lead to a warming trend, with high temperatures rising back into the 
60s for many areas Wednesday and especially Thursday.

&&

.AVIATION /14Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...

Upslope showers will continue over the mountains tonight before
changing to snow showers later today into Saturday. Expect a 
brief period of near-MVFR CIGs at IAD and DCA throughout the 
morning and early afternoon hours, but that should lift just 
after noon at the latest. As for BWI and MTN, those MVFR CIGs 
could be off and on through much of the day, and some showers 
can't even be ruled out (mainly at MTN). All of this will also 
be paired with pretty consistent 20 to 25 knot wind gusts 
throughout the daytime hours. That will taper off into the 
evening hours though.

Sub-VFR conditions will remain over the mountains through 
Saturday as upslope snow showers continue.

Gusts will be out the northwest yet again on Saturday as cold 
air advection funnels in. BKN-OVC stratocumulus deck is expected
each afternoon through Sunday. Northwest winds on Sunday blow 
around 10 knots with gusts between 15 and 20 knots expected. 
Winds diminish overnight with light northwest winds expected on 
Monday. VFR conditions and light winds are then expected Monday 
and Tuesday as high pressure builds toward the area.

&&

.MARINE...

Small Craft Advisories in effect for all waters through this
evening as winds strengthen in the wake of yesterday's frontal
passage. Over the open waters, wind gusts of 30 knots are
expected, with 20 to 25 knots elsewhere. Winds will taper off 
over the Potomac overnight before picking up again on Saturday. 
As such, SCAs were dropped there tonight, but then they are in 
effect again all day Saturday. Winds may diminish some on 
Sunday, but gusts up to 20 knots remain possible, so SCAs likely
will be needed for portions of the waters, if not all of them, 
yet again.

Northwest winds will weaken Sunday night into Monday as high 
pressure approaches, but marginal advisory conditions may 
continue through the day. Sub- advisory winds are likely by 
Monday night and Tuesday as the high builds overhead.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Over the next several days, breezy conditions will continue with
afternoon RH values dipping into the 30s to low 40s in the
valleys. Wouldn't be shocked to see some areas drop lower, perhaps
closer to the upper 20s in the typical dry spots in the valleys
out west following frontal passages. Given recent fire activity
in the past several days, there could be some issues each 
afternoon when winds peak and RHs drop to their lowest. Winds 
will begin to taper off early next week, but RHs will remain 
low, and potentially even be a bit drier, so would not be 
surprised if early next week has a day that needs closer 
attention as well.

&&

.LWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
DC...None.
MD...Small Craft Advisory until 6 PM EST Saturday for MDZ008.
VA...None.
WV...None.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory until 6 PM EST Saturday for ANZ530>534-
     537>543.
     Small Craft Advisory until 6 PM EST this evening for ANZ535-
     536.
     Small Craft Advisory from 9 AM to 6 PM EST Saturday for ANZ535-
     536.

&&

$$
